## Controllers

  
The Steam Frame Controllers have the same capabilities as your standard console gaming controllers plus touch states, grip buttons, capacitive finger tracking, and 6-DOF spatial tracking. This gives you many more options on how to let players interact with your titles. It also allows users to play non-VR content on the headset without a separate device.  
  

## VR Compatibility

While you will always get a better user experience by tailoring your title to the Frame Controllers specifically, our controller compatibility modes have become quite robust. SteamVR will always use a Frame Controller binding by default but in the case one is not available it will first look for a [OpenXR Generic Controller](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.1/html/xrspec.html#XR_KHR_generic_controller) binding, then an [Oculus Touch](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.1/html/xrspec.html#semantic-paths-oculus-touch-controller-profile) binding, and remap those to the Frame Controller layout.   

* The menu button on Oculus Touch will map to the View button at the top of the Steam Frame Controller.
* The top button of the Oculus Touch controllers (B / Y) will map to all three top buttons of the Steam Frame Controllers (Dpad Left, Dpad Up, Dpad Right / X, Y, B).

## Non-VR Compatibility

When playing Non-VR titles locally or via streaming the Frame Controllers take full advantage of [Steam Input](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/steam_controller). Depending on the game and the configured bindings it will show up as a generic gamepad or keyboard/mouse.

## OpenXR Interaction Profile

You'll find an OpenXR Interaction Profile included in each Game Engine plugin (or in the case of Godot in the engine itself). If you have your own custom engine you can add support via our extension detailed on the [steamframe/engines/custom](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/steamframe/engines/custom) documentation page.  
  
To enable the interaction profile you must request to use the extension:   

XR\_VALVE\_frame\_controller\_interaction

  
Then you can suggest bindings for the interaction profile path:  

/interaction\_profiles/valve/frame\_controller\_valve

## OpenVR Bindings

You can bind to the Steam Frame Controllers like you would any other OpenVR controller type. Its **controller\_type** is `"frame_controller"`. They support finger tracking via the [Skeletal Input API](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/openvr/wiki/SteamVR-Skeletal-Input/4db5b685942e4b84f16bb3796143e292ad9226e6) and all of the controls listed above. You can create bindings for it in the SteamVR Binding UI.

## HMD

  
It is unlikely that you will have a reason to need the hmd name, but if you do, its **controller\_type** is `"frame_hmd"`. Be sure NOT to use this for determining the type of controllers the user currently has. Many users choose to mix and match hmds and controllers.

## Eye Tracking

## OpenXR

Our current support for eye tracking uses the **XR\_EXT\_eye\_gaze\_interaction** OpenXR extension. You can find details about that on the [OpenXR spec site here](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.0/html/xrspec.html#XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction).

## OpenVR

OpenVR has two functions in IVRInput **GetEyeTrackingDataRelativeToNow** and **GetEyeTrackingDataForNextFrame**. To use those you will need to create a new action of type `"eyetracking"` to pass into the functions.
